question.prompt: A biased die is rolled. Can 1/6 be used as the probability of rolling a 6? Why?

solutions.explanation: The value 1/6 is calculated using \(P=m/n\), which requires all outcomes to be equally likely. When the die is biased, the scores are not equally likely, so 1/6 cannot be used directly.
